reasoning: Wrong-reference (invented flags), filed at P4 per doc-severity ruling (2026-09-30). ~/.hermes/scripts/bunker-qa.sh line 16: 'bunker-qa.sh run <repo-dir> [--server X] [--ttl 4h] [--keep]' and line 19 similar for launch. The parsers (lines 2147-2150 run(), 2259-2262 launch()) accept ONLY --keep; run "$2" "${@:3}" forwards args to run(), which loops 'for a in "$@"; do [ "$a" = "--keep" ]...' — a --server or --ttl argument is silently IGNORED and the battery runs against the default server with default TTL. This is the documented-flag-the-binary-rejects class (help-text-as-oracle rule), except worse: not rejected, silently dropped. Evidence command: grep -n -- '--server\|--ttl' ~/.hermes/scripts/bunker-qa.sh (flags appear ONLY in the header comment and inside bunker CLI calls, never in arg parsing). Correct invocation is env-based: BUNKER_QA_SERVER=<srv> BUNKER_QA_TTL=4h bunker-qa.sh run <repo> (matches qa-foreman skill §623 and server-selection-ladder.md). Reader: operator dispatching a battery. Artifact: bunker-qa.sh lines 15-23 Usage block. Acceptance: the Usage block shows env-var overrides (BUNKER_QA_SERVER/BUNKER_QA_TTL) instead of flags, or the parsers actually accept the flags; a reader copying the documented invocation gets the server they asked for.
title: P4 — fix rot: bunker-qa.sh Usage block documents --server/--ttl flags that run/launch do not parse
